paragraphs.paragraph: David's Words on Rule and Covenant
paragraphs.title: David's Words on Rule and Covenant

answers: The anointed of the God of Jacob and the sweet psalmist of Israel
A Philistine captain
A priest in the temple
easy.explanation: David is called the anointed of the God of Jacob and the sweet psalmist of Israel.
easy.q: How does David describe himself in these words?

answers: The people
The Spirit of the LORD
The captains
easy.explanation: David says, “The Spirit of the LORD spake by me.”

answers: Living waters
Fruit trees
Thorns
easy.explanation: The sons of Belial are compared to thorns that are burned with fire.
easy.q: What are the sons of Belial compared to?

answers: A rich and powerful ruler
A just ruler who rules in the fear of God
A ruler who acts alone
medium.explanation: The passage says that he who rules over men must be just and rule in the fear of God.
medium.q: What kind of ruler is presented as worthy to rule over men?

answers: The just ruler
The sons of Belial
The weapons of war
medium.explanation: The righteous ruler is described with the bright and life-giving images of morning light and tender grass.
medium.q: What is compared to the light of the morning and tender grass after rain?

answers: Dangerous men who must be destroyed
Men who keep the covenant
Men who bring rain
medium.explanation: The thorns represent the sons of Belial, who cannot be safely handled and are burned.
medium.q: In context, what does “thorns thrust away” describe?

answers: David's house is connected with an ordered covenant, while the sons of Belial are like thorns to be burned
David's house is devoted to war, while the sons of Belial are devoted to singing
David's house is in the field, while the sons of Belial are in the city
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the sure covenant with the worthless and dangerous sons of Belial.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between David's house and the sons of Belial?

answers: David's words are presented as spoken by divine inspiration
David speaks only about ordinary daily life
David says that he is unable to speak
challenge.explanation: David says that the Spirit of the LORD spoke by him and that God's word was in his tongue.
challenge.q: What does the connection between the Spirit of the LORD and David's words suggest?

answers: The covenant is stable and firmly established
The covenant lasts only a short time
The covenant concerns only the sons of Belial
challenge.explanation: The words everlasting, ordered, and sure emphasize the covenant's permanence and reliability.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the phrase “an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure”?

paragraphs.idea: David's Words on Rule and Covenant

answers: The Tachmonite, Eleazar, and Shammah
Abishai, Benaiah, and Uriah
Joab, David, and Ahithophel
easy.explanation: The account begins with the Tachmonite, Eleazar, and Shammah.
easy.q: Who were the first three mighty warriors named in the list?

answers: The Egyptians
The Philistines
The Ammonites
A cave
A well
A piece of ground full of lentiles
easy.explanation: Shammah stood in the midst of a field of lentiles and defended it.
easy.q: What did Shammah defend from the Philistines?

answers: He slew eight hundred at one time
He brought water to David
He guarded a well in Bethlehem
medium.explanation: He lifted up his spear against eight hundred and slew them at one time.
medium.q: What great deed is attributed to the Tachmonite?

answers: He lost his sword in a well
His hand clave unto the sword
He dropped his spear in the field
medium.explanation: His hand clave unto the sword after he fought until his hand was weary.
medium.q: What happened to Eleazar's hand during the battle?

answers: He remained standing and held his position
He fell asleep in the field
He left the battle
medium.explanation: Shammah stayed in the field and defended it instead of fleeing.
medium.q: What does “he stood in the midst of the ground” mean in context?

answers: Each stood against many enemies and helped bring a great victory
All three brought water to David
All three served only as commanders
challenge.explanation: Each warrior is portrayed as standing firm against overwhelming opposition and achieving victory.
challenge.q: What do the accounts of the three warriors have in common?

answers: Shammah showed personal courage by defending the ground despite the people's retreat
Shammah did not take part in the battle
The Philistines helped Shammah
challenge.explanation: The people fled, but Shammah stood and defended the field.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the people fleeing while Shammah remained in the field?

answers: Their courageous actions were followed by the LORD's great victory
They won without any mention of divine help
They took no action until the people returned
challenge.explanation: The text specifically says that the LORD wrought a great victory after their stand.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the deeds of Eleazar and Shammah and the great victory?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Three and Their Devotion to David
paragraphs.title: The Three and Their Devotion to David

answers: Water from the well of Bethlehem
Wine from a vineyard
Water from the Jordan
easy.explanation: David longed for water from the well of Bethlehem by the gate.
easy.q: What did David desire to drink?

answers: They waited for the Philistines to leave
They brake through the host of the Philistines and drew water
They dug a new well
easy.explanation: They broke through the Philistine host and drew water from the well.
easy.q: What did the three mighty men do to obtain the water?

answers: He drank it all
He divided it among the people
He refused to drink it and poured it out unto the LORD
easy.explanation: David would not drink it, but poured it out unto the LORD.
easy.q: What did David do with the water they brought him?

answers: It was salty
He regarded it as the blood of men who had put their lives in jeopardy
It belonged to the Philistines
medium.explanation: David said it was the blood of the men who went in jeopardy of their lives.
medium.q: Why did David refuse to drink the water?

answers: He despised their deed
He honored their devotion by offering the water unto the LORD
He demanded that they bring more water
medium.explanation: By refusing to drink and pouring out the water, David treated their sacrifice as sacred.
medium.q: What does David's action show about his attitude toward the warriors' deed?

answers: They forced their way through the army
They hid among the soldiers
They left the battlefield
medium.explanation: The phrase means that they broke through the Philistine camp to reach the well.
medium.q: What does “brake through the host” mean?

answers: A simple desire of David became for them a dangerous act of devotion
David commanded them to begin a war against the Philistines
The three men asked David to drink with them
challenge.explanation: David merely expressed his longing, but the three risked their lives to fulfill it.
challenge.q: What connection is there between David's desire and the deed of the three warriors?

answers: The water represented the danger and sacrifice the warriors had endured
The water was red because of Bethlehem's soil
The warriors were wounded inside the well
challenge.explanation: David viewed the water as representing the lives placed in jeopardy to obtain it.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “the blood of the men” signify in this context?

answers: He was chief among them and had a distinguished name
He was one of the first three
He did not participate in battle
challenge.explanation: Abishai was chief among the other three and was their captain.
challenge.q: What position did Abishai hold among the other three?

paragraphs.idea: The Three and Their Devotion to David

paragraphs.paragraph: Benaiah and the Rank of the Warriors
paragraphs.title: Benaiah and the Rank of the Warriors

answers: The son of Jehoiada
The son of Ahithophel
The son of Zeruiah
easy.explanation: Benaiah is identified as the son of Jehoiada.

answers: Bringing water and writing the list
Slaying Moabite warriors, a lion, and an Egyptian
Defending only the field of lentiles
easy.explanation: The passage records Benaiah's victories over Moabites, a lion, and an Egyptian.
easy.q: For which deeds was Benaiah known?

answers: David
Eleazar
Shammah
easy.explanation: David set Benaiah over his guard.
easy.q: Who set Benaiah over his guard?

answers: He slew a lion in the midst of a pit
He defended the field of lentiles
He drew water from Bethlehem
medium.explanation: Benaiah went down and slew a lion in a pit in time of snow.
medium.q: What did Benaiah do in the time of snow?

answers: He took the Egyptian's spear and slew him with it
He fled from him into the pit
He asked Abishai to strike him
medium.explanation: Benaiah plucked the spear from the Egyptian's hand and killed him with his own spear.
medium.q: How did Benaiah kill the Egyptian?

answers: Benaiah did not reach the rank of the foremost three warriors
Benaiah took part in no battles
Benaiah was unknown to David
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Benaiah's rank was below that of the first three.
medium.q: What does “he attained not unto the first three” mean?

answers: He was more honourable than the thirty but did not attain unto the first three
He was below the thirty and one of the first three
He was equal in rank to every warrior
challenge.explanation: The passage says he was more honourable than the thirty, but did not attain unto the first three.
challenge.q: How is Benaiah's rank described in relation to the groups of warriors?

answers: His courage was tested against warriors, a beast, and difficult conditions
He excelled only in administration
He fought only within Israel's camp
challenge.explanation: His deeds include fighting Moabites, a lion, and an Egyptian, including during snow.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the variety of Benaiah's exploits?

answers: His exploits and distinguished rank help explain why David placed him over his guard
David appointed him because he never fought in battle
He was appointed because he was one of the first three
challenge.explanation: The account presents Benaiah's mighty deeds and honorable rank before describing David's appointment.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between Benaiah's courage and his appointment by David?

paragraphs.idea: Benaiah and the Rank of the Warriors

paragraphs.paragraph: The List of the Thirty Warriors
paragraphs.title: The List of the Thirty Warriors

answers: A list of mighty warriors
A description of the building of the tabernacle
A speech by Samuel
easy.explanation: These verses list additional mighty men who served David.

answers: Uriah the Hittite
The Tachmonite
Shammah the Hararite
easy.explanation: The list ends with Uriah the Hittite.
easy.q: Who appears at the end of the list?

answers: Thirty
Thirty and seven
Eight hundred
easy.explanation: The final statement says, “thirty and seven in all.”
easy.q: How many are mentioned in the final total?

answers: Their place of origin or family affiliation
The number of enemies each man slew
The amount of money each man received
medium.explanation: Many names are accompanied by a city, region, family, or ethnic affiliation.
medium.q: What kind of detail appears alongside many of the names?

answers: Nahari the Beerothite
Elhanan the son of Dodo
Uriah the Hittite
medium.explanation: Nahari the Beerothite is identified as armourbearer to Joab.
medium.q: Who is described as Joab's armourbearer?

answers: Uriah's ethnic or national affiliation
Uriah's duty as an armourbearer
The place where Uriah kept a well
medium.explanation: The title identifies Uriah's Hittite affiliation.
medium.q: What does “the Hittite” indicate in the phrase “Uriah the Hittite”?

answers: Mighty deeds and service are attributed to a broad group, not only to the first three
Only three warriors served David
The list concerns only the kings of Israel
challenge.explanation: After the foremost warriors, the passage records many additional men.
challenge.q: What does the presence of many names in the list show?

answers: By giving different names, cities, families, and national affiliations
By describing one identical battle for every man
By giving only their ages
challenge.explanation: The accompanying details identify varied places, families, and origins.
challenge.q: How does the list emphasize variety among the warriors?

answers: The final total includes additional men beyond the group called the thirty
The list contains no names
Every warrior was named seven times
challenge.explanation: Although the group is called the thirty, the final total is thirty-seven.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the difference between “the thirty” and the final total of thirty-seven?

paragraphs.idea: The List of the Thirty Warriors
